hfintro: Orient yourself among NLP tasks, model families, and the training workflow.
gpt2: Follow tokens through a decoder-only model and understand how next-token predictions are produced.
smol: Follow a real model through data decisions, pretraining, post-training, and infrastructure debugging.
production: Connect model capabilities to evaluation, latency, cost, tools, and application design.
foundation: On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models
Understand the foundation-model framing, adaptation opportunities, and systemic limitations.
transformer: Build intuition for encoder-decoder architecture, attention, positional information, and output probabilities.
linear: Practice tensor shapes, matrix operations, reductions, dot products, and norms in code.
maps: Connect vector spaces, linear transformations, bases, and rank to matrix computations.
info: Understand entropy, cross-entropy, and KL divergence through probability diagrams.
prob: Work through random variables, conditional probabilities, expectations, and sampling.
backprop: See why reverse-mode differentiation efficiently accumulates derivatives through a computation graph.
csback: Trace gradients through scalar and vector operations and implement the chain rule.
momentum: Explore how curvature, learning rate, and momentum change optimization trajectories.
optim: An overview of gradient descent optimization algorithms
Compare SGD, momentum, adaptive optimizers, and practical optimization difficulties.
general: Separate training fit from generalization and reason about model capacity and data.
nn: But what is a Neural Network?
Build intuition for weights, activations, layers, and learned representations.
csnn: Understand activations, feed-forward computation, network depth, and representational capacity.
cssetup: Connect preprocessing, initialization, regularization, and loss functions to training behavior.
transfer: Distinguish frozen feature extraction from fine-tuning; examples use vision networks.
word2vec: Understand learned embeddings, similarity, context prediction, and negative sampling.
